sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Alpharetta, GA?
sections.html:
Alpharetta owners deal with two billing offices. The Fulton County Tax Commissioner collects for Fulton County government, the schools and the State of Georgia. The City of Alpharetta handles its own city tax: its website lists Property Tax Accounts among its payment options and Homestead Exemptions among its applications, and the Tax Commissioner's list of cities it collects for names Atlanta, Mountain Park, Sandy Springs, Johns Creek and Chattahoochee Hills, not Alpharetta.

The Fulton County Board of Tax Assessors sets the value on which both bills rely. Georgia's Department of Revenue explains the general rule: where a city bills separately, the city clerk or finance office collects the city tax, while the county collects the county and school taxes. Check your parcel's tax bill and your city bill so you pay each to the right office.

The Tax Commissioner runs a customer service center at 11575 Maxwell Road in Alpharetta, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county tax line is 404-613-6100.

sections.h2: Why were the 2026 Fulton County tax bills different?
sections.html:
The 2026 digest was late. On July 15, 2026 the county commissioners learned that the Board of Assessors had not yet processed an unprecedented number of land packages, which delayed submitting the digest to the Georgia Department of Revenue for certification. The Superior Court of Fulton County granted a petition on August 4, 2026 allowing temporary bills based on 2025 millage rates and the digest assembled so far.

Those estimated bills went out on August 15 with an October 15 due date for Fulton County. Each taxing jurisdiction sets its final millage rate once the digest is done, and the county said that either a refund or a revised final bill will be issued if needed. That due date has passed, so owners who paid the estimate should watch for a corrected bill.

For the City of Alpharetta portion, read the due date printed on the city bill or ask the city Finance Department.

sections.h2: What do I do with each Alpharetta tax office?
sections.html:
Who handles what for a house in Alpharetta
QuestionOffice to ask
Value and assessment appealsFulton County Board of Tax Assessors
County and school tax bill and paymentFulton County Tax Commissioner
City of Alpharetta tax bill and city homestead filingCity of Alpharetta Finance Department
Deed recording and transfer tax certificationClerk of Superior Court

Source: Fulton County Tax Commissioner and the Georgia Department of Revenue transfer tax page.

The Department of Revenue says the county tax office is the place for payment, homestead filing in many counties, and returns, while the assessor handles value appeals. Appeals go in writing to the assessors within 45 days of the notice mailing, and you choose among the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer and an arbitrator.

sections.h2: What do I need to know about homestead and returns in Alpharetta?
sections.html:
Georgia's standard homestead exemption subtracts $2,000 from assessed value, and assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value. Georgia's County Property Tax Facts page for Fulton says a homestead application may be made at any time after the home becomes your primary residence, up to April 1 of the first year you want it. Skipping the application counts as a waiver.

Property tax returns are filed between January 1 and April 1. A taxpayer who skips the return is treated as having filed the same return as the year before. Because Alpharetta runs its own homestead filing, make sure both the city and the county have your exemption on file.

  • Check the county bill for the exemption line.
  • Check the city bill for the city exemption line.
  • Confirm both offices have the correct mailing address after a sale.

sections.h2: What should I know about Alpharetta itself before selling?
sections.html:
Alpharetta sits in northern Fulton County, about 26 miles north of downtown Atlanta. It covers 27.3 square miles and borders Johns Creek, Roswell, Milton and unincorporated Forsyth County. The city was chartered in 1858, served as seat of Milton County until 1931, and then came under Fulton County when the two counties merged during the Depression.

The 2020 census counted 65,818 residents, 24,727 households and 26,089 housing units, 5.2 percent of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.2 percent. Fulton County Schools serve the city, with Alpharetta High School serving most of it. Avalon, North Point Mall and the downtown City Center anchor retail, and McKesson and Travelers have offices here, along with a cluster of data centers.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes when an Alpharetta house sells?
sections.html:
Georgia charges the year's tax to the person who owned the property on January 1, and no refund is available to a partial year owner. Transfer tax must be paid before the Clerk of Superior Court records the deed, and the seller is liable under state law unless the contract moves the cost. Sellers file the PT-61 declaration online through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

The Department of Revenue says county tax liens are filed in the clerk's office on the general execution docket. Before listing, ask both the Tax Commissioner and the city for a statement of any balance, including any estimated 2026 payment still open.

sections.h2: How do I look up and pay the Fulton County part of the bill?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner takes the appraised value and exemption status from the Board of Tax Assessors, applies the millage rates set by the Board of Commissioners and other governing authorities, and mails bills to the owner address the assessors provide. That last point matters after a sale or inheritance: if the assessors have an old address, the bill goes there.

The Tax Commissioner's website offers two ways to find a bill, and you can pay on the same system by credit or debit card or by e-check:

  • Search for a tax bill using a full or partial parcel ID, an account number or a street address.
  • Request a tax summary for several parcels at once when you have the complete parcel IDs.

In person, the Maxwell Road center is the closest to Alpharetta. The county also keeps a downtown office at 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113 in Atlanta, and a North Fulton Service Center at 7741 Roswell Road NE in Sandy Springs. All of them list the same weekday hours and the 404-613-6100 number.

sections.h2: Can I recover tax that was assessed or collected in error?
sections.html:
You may ask for a refund in writing. Georgia's county property tax facts say refund claims for taxes erroneously or illegally assessed and collected must begin within three years of payment. When an assessment appeal ends with a lower value, the refund is processed automatically as soon as the final taxable value is set.

This ties directly to the 2026 temporary bills. Because they used 2025 millage rates and a partial digest, a revised final bill or refund may follow, and the county says so in its own announcement. Keep the receipt for any payment made on the estimate and compare it with the final bill before the house closes.

Georgia also taxes the recording of a long-term note secured by real estate, at $1.50 for each $500 or fractional part of the face amount, and the security instrument must be recorded within 90 days. Ask the Clerk of Superior Court who collects it in Fulton County.

faqs.q: Does the Fulton County Tax Commissioner collect Alpharetta city tax?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner lists the cities it collects for, and Alpharetta is not among them. The City of Alpharetta handles its own property tax accounts.

faqs.q: When was the 2026 Fulton County estimated bill due?
faqs.a: The county due date was October 15, 2026. Bills were temporary estimates issued under a Superior Court order, and a refund or revised bill may follow.

faqs.q: Where is the Fulton Tax Commissioner's office in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: At 11575 Maxwell Road, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone is 404-613-6100.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Alpharetta assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice, and the appeal goes to the Fulton County Board of Tax Assessors.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Alpharetta sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under Georgia law, although contracts commonly shift the payment to the buyer.
